rejected_videos.reason: No clean, prerequisite-safe segment exists. The class-method explanation depends on the earlier shared dogs class variable, introducing blocked python.instance_vs_class_attributes, and never demonstrates the required alternative constructor using return cls(arguments) (f2). The static-method explanation contains a factual error: at 342–346 it claims that not receiving the class means a static method cannot reference anything within the class, and at 415–443 it repeats that class attributes and methods are inaccessible. Static methods receive no implicit instance or class argument, but can access class attributes and methods through an explicit class reference. This is a technical contradiction, not merely missing coverage. The later example also introduces blocked python.local_modules at 470–476. Trimming cannot retain a complete standalone explanation of the intended binding choice while avoiding these problems.

No clean segment meets the required teaching objective. The example stores Engine and Wheel objects in instance attributes (f1), but only reads their attributes; it never delegates work through self.collaborator.method(arguments) (f2). The video also makes misleading Python lifetime claims: at 18–24 seconds it says components cannot exist independently, and at 407–415 seconds it claims deleting the cars would make their engines and wheels stop existing. Constructing components inside a constructor does not enforce exclusive ownership or prevent other references from keeping them alive. Trimming those statements would still leave the required delegation example absent.

No clean, prerequisite-safe standalone range covers both required facts. The complete example begins at 0, but introduces untaught inheritance and is-a relationships at 47–58 and returns to inheritance at 102. Technical-accuracy rejection: at 27–31 seconds, repeated at 216–220 seconds, the video incorrectly says super() returns a temporary object of a parent class. It returns a proxy that delegates lookup to the next class in the method resolution order, not a parent-class instance. The live-code example at 37–212 seconds demonstrates inherited initialization and retaining derived height initialization (f3), but omits the required MRO explanation (f2) and does not explain ordinary overridden-method lookup (f1). Trimming away the incorrect definition would not provide a complete, accurate lesson covering the required facts.

The video contains a factual error: at 108–111 seconds it says each object will have its own copy of the class variable. This contradicts the shared-state distinction required by f1. The video also never demonstrates a shared mutable class-body list (f2) or self.items = [] in __init__ to create separate per-instance lists (f3). An earlier trimmed range could provide partial f1 coverage, but would neither address these required mutable-state facts nor resolve the video's misleading ownership model.
